title: Toxic-exposure records are increasingly used for claims and care while veteran self-access and correction remain in rollout
source_unit: GAO-26-108483, Military Health Care: Information on Use of and Access to Toxic Exposure Records
geography: United States; Department of Defense and Department of Veterans Affairs Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record system

observations.period: October 2019-January 2026 ILER staff-use data; access rollout through October 2026 plans; report published July 22, 2026

denominator.unit: veterans screened since 2022 in the VA estimate cited by GAO

potential_exposure.value: about 48% of veterans screened since 2022, approximately 3.2 million of 6.8 million, had at least one potential toxic exposure

record_purpose.value: ILER links military exposure and related information from DOD and VA databases for clinical decisions, health research, and disability-claims processing

post_act_use.value: use increased after the August 2022 PACT Act, driven largely by Veterans Benefits Administration staff, who were the largest user group
post_act_use.unit: ILER account logins by staff group

self_access.value: service members gained access and the ability to add self-reported updates in March 2026; officials planned correction requests for service members by September 2026 and veteran access/correction by October 2026

potential_benefit_and_risk.value: stakeholder organizations identified greater transparency and more informed clinician conversations as potential benefits, while warning that missing or incomplete records could create frustration

observations.method: GAO analyzed DOD and VA ILER staff-use data from October 2019 through January 2026, reviewed documents, interviewed ILER officials, and interviewed eight selected stakeholder organizations.
observations.uncertainty: The 48% exposure figure is a VA estimate among screened veterans and is not a prevalence estimate for all veterans. Login shares do not establish claim approval, care receipt, diagnosis, health improvement, correction success, or household outcomes. Stakeholder interviews are selected and nongeneralizable.
observations.subgroup: Service members, veterans, DOD and VA staff, Veterans Benefits Administration claims staff, clinicians, researchers, and selected military/veteran and toxic-exposure organizations; these are distinct users and populations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Increased VBA use may reflect the PACT Act's expanded eligibility and administrative demand rather than worsening exposure or record quality. Self-reported updates may improve completeness but do not by themselves verify exposure or establish benefit eligibility.

related_sources.claim: Accessible report contains ILER use, exposure-screening, access, correction, and interview context.
VA PACT Act context is related to expanded health-care and disability-benefit eligibility for qualifying toxic exposures.

boundary: This record captures a data-governance, access, and institutional-use route for toxic-exposure records. It does not establish individual exposure verification, claim approval, treatment, health improvement, correction success, trust, or political action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO landing page and accessible report reviewed; underlying ILER logs, VA screening records, and stakeholder interview materials are not retained.
